title: Magnetic Order from First-Principles Linear Response
authors: Yaroslav Zhumagulov, Emiliano Cruz-Aranda, Denis Kochan, Oleg V. Yazyev
abstract: The magnetic order of a material is usually predicted by comparing the energies of trial spin configurations, a strategy that cannot reach orders outside the chosen set and rapidly becomes intractable as the number of magnetic sites grows. We show that the order can instead be identified directly from the paramagnetic state: the leading eigenmodes of its self-consistent magnetization response, obtained with spin--orbit coupling at arbitrary wavevector within the primitive cell, determine both the ordering wavevector and the pattern of moments, with no candidate configurations. With no prior assumption about the order, the method correctly reproduces the G-type stacking with out-of-plane moments in the altermagnet candidate KV$_2$Se$_2$O, the $3{:}1$ ferrimagnetic tetrahedra of Cu$_2$OSeO$_3$, and the incommensurate spiral instability of monolayer NiI$_2$. Our results establish the response of the paramagnetic state as a predictive and unbiased route to assessing magnetic order, enabling systematic searches for complex magnets.
summary: This work presents a novel, unbiased theoretical method to predict magnetic order by analyzing the leading eigenmodes of the magnetization response within the paramagnetic state. By applying this technique to materials like $	ext{KV}_2	ext{Se}_2	ext{O}$ and $	ext{NiI}_2$, the authors successfully reproduce complex magnetic structures without needing to assume the final ordered state beforehand.
main_problem: Traditional methods for predicting magnetic order are limited to predefined spin configurations and become computationally intractable for large systems.
main_result: The magnetic order can be predicted unbiasedly by analyzing the leading eigenmodes of the self-consistent magnetization response calculated from the paramagnetic state.
method: The method involves solving a linearized eigenvalue problem derived from the self-consistent magnetization response function, incorporating spin-orbit coupling.
model_or_system: The study applies this method to various magnetic materials, including $	ext{KV}_2	ext{Se}_2	ext{O}$, $	ext{Cu}_2	ext{OSeO}_3$, and monolayer $	ext{NiI}_2$, which are characterized by complex magnetic interactions.
key_observables: The largest eigenvalue ($\lambda_{\mathbf{q}}$) and its corresponding eigenvector ($ oldsymbol{\phi}_{\mathbf{q}}$) determine the magnetic instability, wavevector ($\mathbf{q}$), and pattern of magnetic moments.
important_parameters: Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC), wavevector ($\mathbf{q}$), and the instability threshold ($\lambda_{\mathbf{q}} = 1$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the leading eigenmodes of the paramagnetic state response are sufficient to capture the true magnetic ground state, overcoming the limitations of pre-selected configurations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the leading response eigenvectors for $	ext{KV}_2	ext{Se}_2	ext{O}$ for both C-type and G-type stacking, visualizing the magnetization components.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the limitations of prior methods, details the theoretical framework using linear response theory on the paramagnetic state, and then applies this framework to calculate and distinguish between known magnetic orders in several distinct materials.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the use of linear response theory to probe instabilities from a non-interacting (paramagnetic) reference state is a powerful, generalizable technique for identifying emergent collective behavior, which has parallels in open quantum system dynamics.

FIG. 2. Leading Γ-point response eigenvectors of Cu2OSeO3: (a) the state of the threefold-degenerate T mode whose net moment points along [111] and (b) the nearly degenerate, fully symmetric A mode. A cubic Cu2OSeO3 cell holds the four Cu4 tetrahedra. Each tetrahedron has one Cu1 site at the 4a Wyckoff position (blue) and three Cu2 sites at the 12b position (red). Arrows indicate the site magnetic moments: in each tetrahedron, for both modes, the blue moment is directed opposite to the sum of the three red moments, corresponding to a 3:1 ferrimagnetic configuration. In the A mode, the four moments of the tetrahedron are directed along the four ⟨111⟩-type directions and mutually cancel out.
